judge_panel.matching_evidence:
[mathematical] Incorrect normalization factor in the timelike “slowness” function, Sec. 3, Eqs. (54), (63), and (64)

**What is wrong:** Eq. (54) gives
\[
\int \Theta ds
=\int \frac{3\,d\gamma}{1-\gamma^2}
=\frac32\ln\left(\frac{\gamma+1}{\gamma-1}\right).
\tag{54}
\]
But in the theorem the paper defines
\[
F(\gamma)=\frac23\ln\left(\frac{\gamma+1}{\gamma-1}\right)
\tag{64}
\]
...
The factor in Eq. (64) is inconsistent with Eq. (54). If \(\Theta\) is the expansion scalar, the coefficient following from Eq. (54) is \(3/2\), not \(2/3\).

**Concrete fix:** Replace Eq. (64) by
\[
F(\gamma)=\frac32\ln\left(\frac{\gamma+1}{\gamma-1}\right)
\]
judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer explicitly identifies the exact mismatched coefficient 2/3 versus 3/2 in the same F(gamma) expression and locates the internal inconsistency.
